skill.name: pixi-package-manager
skill.description: Guides setup, migration, and troubleshooting for Pixi package manager workflows in scientific Python projects.
skill.summary: Use Pixi to build reproducible conda and PyPI environments for scientific Python.
skill.author: CodingKaiser

security_audit.summary: The audit confirms one critical supply-chain issue: a CI example pipes a remote Pixi installer directly into bash. It also confirms medium-risk shell-hook eval guidance; the remaining static matches are markdown examples, resource links, placeholder paths, or prose-only false positives.

remediation.issue: Remote installer is piped directly to bash in the GitLab CI example.
remediation.suggestion: Replace the curl-to-bash pattern with a trusted setup action, a pinned release, or a verified installer with checksum or signature validation.

remediation.issue: Shell-hook output is evaluated in script guidance.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer pixi run for automation. If shell-hook is necessary, call a trusted Pixi binary and explain why evaluation is acceptable.

remediation.issue: Example dependency sources include placeholders for remote Git repositories.
remediation.suggestion: Add guidance to pin Git dependencies to trusted commits and review lockfile changes before merging.

content.value_statement: Scientific Python teams often need reproducible environments across conda and PyPI packages. This skill gives practical Pixi workflows for setup, dependency groups, tasks, migration, and CI.
actual_capabilities: Plan new Pixi projects that use pyproject.toml and pixi.lock.
Choose conda-forge or PyPI dependencies based on package type and platform needs.
Organize features, environments, and tasks for development, testing, and production.
Migrate requirements.txt or environment.yml workflows into Pixi projects.
Design CI workflows that install dependencies, run tests, and use lockfiles.
Troubleshoot solver, build, activation, and lockfile problems.
limitations: Pixi must already be installed or available in the target environment.
The skill does not verify third-party package safety or repository trust.
Complex scientific stacks may still need platform-specific constraints.
Package availability depends on configured channels and operating systems.

use_cases.title: Start a Research Project
use_cases.description: Create a reproducible Pixi environment for notebooks, tests, and scientific libraries.

use_cases.title: Migrate Existing Dependencies
use_cases.description: Convert requirements.txt or environment.yml workflows into a cleaner Pixi project layout.

use_cases.title: Standardize CI Environments
use_cases.description: Use lockfiles and Pixi tasks to make test and build jobs more repeatable.

prompt_templates.title: Create a New Pixi Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Pixi setup plan for a new scientific Python project. Include dependencies, environments, tasks, and files I should commit.

prompt_templates.title: Migrate Existing Dependencies
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current dependency list and propose a Pixi migration plan. Separate conda-forge packages, PyPI packages, dev tools, and optional features.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Environment Tasks
prompt_templates.prompt: Design Pixi environments and tasks for development, testing, documentation, and production. Explain how each environment should be used.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize Pixi CI
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my CI workflow for Pixi. Recommend safer installation, caching, lockfile use, and task structure for reliable builds.

output_examples.input: I need a Pixi setup for geospatial analysis.
output_examples.output: A project plan that separates core geospatial dependencies, development tools, notebooks, and repeatable data-processing tasks.

output_examples.input: I have a requirements.txt file and want to move to Pixi.
output_examples.output: A migration checklist that maps packages to conda-forge or PyPI, identifies risky pins, and suggests review steps before committing.

output_examples.input: My CI job is slow and inconsistent.
output_examples.output: A CI improvement plan covering lockfile usage, cache strategy, safer Pixi installation, and task-based test execution.

best_practices: Commit pixi.lock and review lockfile changes in pull requests.
Use conda-forge for compiled scientific dependencies and PyPI for pure Python gaps.
Prefer pixi run tasks for automation so environments are explicit and repeatable.
anti_patterns: Do not mix unmanaged pip installs into a Pixi environment without tracking them.
Do not use broad version ranges for critical production or research dependencies.
Do not execute remote installers in CI without verification or a trusted setup action.

faq.question: What is Pixi used for?
faq.answer: Pixi manages reproducible project environments that can combine conda-forge packages, PyPI packages, tasks, and lockfiles.

faq.question: Does this replace conda?
faq.answer: It can replace many conda or mamba workflows while still using the conda-forge package ecosystem.

faq.question: Can it work with PyPI packages?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill explains when to use PyPI dependencies and how to keep them organized with Pixi.

faq.question: Is this useful for CI?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers lockfiles, tasks, and repeatable environment setup for test and build pipelines.

faq.question: Can it audit package vulnerabilities?
faq.answer: No. It can recommend dependency hygiene, but vulnerability scanning needs dedicated security tools.

faq.question: Does it install Pixi automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow guidance and examples. Installation should use a trusted, verified method.
